newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canadian killed in train blast was moving to Paris.
newsitem.headline: Canadian killed in train blast was moving to Paris.

text.p: A Canadian woman killed in a Paris train blast this week had been flat-hunting in the capital with her companion, who was wounded in the explosion, the Canadian embassy said Thursday.
An embassy spokesman named the woman, one of two people killed by the Tuesday explosion on a regional express train at Port Royal station, as Helene Viel and her companion as Frank Stonebanks.

French officials have said 41-year-old Lucien Devambez, a Frenchman from New Caledonia, also died in the evening rush hour attack which bore the hallmarks of Algerian Moslem fundamentalists. Eighty-eight people were injured or left in shock by the bombing.

Viel and Stonebanks, both in their thirties, had been searching for a flat in the French capital after he was sent to Paris by his employer, U.S. firm Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, the American subsidiary of France's pharmaceuticals giant Rhone-Poulenc.
Viel, from Riviere-du-Loup in Quebec, and Stonebanks, from British Columbia on the west coast, had been living in a Montreal suburb.
